lesson.summary: Introduction to C: History, Characteristics and Classification
points: Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Labs in the early 1970s, building on B in the Unix environment.
C is general purpose, procedural and imperative; it is normally compiled.
Portability needs care with implementation-dependent behavior. Middle-level is an informal classroom label, not an ISO language category.

archive_evidence.history: C kept the ability to name and call procedures from its predecessors. Its type system let a declaration also describe a function's result type.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: Stephen Johnson worked on pcc, a compiler designed so that it could be adapted to a new machine more easily.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: C supports procedural programming. Functions organize ordered steps that can be called and reused. Procedural and object-oriented describe distinct ways of organizing a program.
archive_evidence.source: GNU C Language Introduction and Reference Manual

archive_evidence.history: A call runs a function's instructions. A function with a return value can pass a result back so the caller can use it.
archive_evidence.source: GNU C Language Introduction and Reference Manual

archive_evidence.history: A function that computes a subtotal can be called from several places. Changing the calculation in that function updates every use of it.
archive_evidence.source: GNU C Language Introduction and Reference Manual
